newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore gas oil, jet fuel, fuel oil trade firm.
newsitem.headline: Singapore gas oil, jet fuel, fuel oil trade firm.

text.p: Singapore oil products market was steady to firm on Thursday, with gas oil, jet fuel and fuel oil traded at high levels, traders said.

They said 20,000 tonnes of 180-cst fuel oil traded at a five-year high of $124 a tonne for October 24-28 lifting between a European major and a Singapore trader. Traders said the strong fuel oil price is caused more by high crude and gas oil values, as supplies are plentiful while regional demand is steady. Chinese buyers would be spooked by high fuel oil prices, traders said. Gas oil again traded at $29.80 a barrel for 220,000 barrels lifting Oct 24-28 between a Japanese and a Thai trader.

The Japanese trader remained keen to buy an identical cargo at the same price. A major that sold a cargo Tuesday offered an end-Oct cargo at $30.50. Traders said gas oil prices are expected to maintain its uptrend on tightening MidEast supplies.

Jet fuel was sold at $30 a barrel by a Mediterranean trader for Oct 24-28. A major offered at $31.15 for early November. Traders said the premium jet fuel holds over gas oil is not expected to last as jet demand remained depressed. Taiwan bought by tender two jet cargoes at $246.95 a tonne for end-October/mid-November arrival from a Mediterranean trader and a MidEast trader.

Naphtha firmed on fundamentals and strong western markets, traders said. Singapore remained tight in early November with full-range heard sold at a 90-cent premium to Singapore quotes while 0.66 SG fetched a 60-cent premium (on a 9-conversion). Paper bids for second-half October rose 50 cents to $22.50. Vitol made the best bid for 125,000 barrels of light naphtha from Sri Lanka at $1.18 below Singapore quotes, lifting October 19-20. Taiwan might cancel its purchase for November on high offers of over $230 a tonne. The gasoline bid for 92-octane unleaded rose 20 cents to $24.25 a barrel fob for Oct 24-28 but no sellers appeared. -- Singapore newsroom (65-870-3084)
